title: Review each item after real use
statement: Once items are in use, review each one's statistics as a standing duty, and revise, quarantine or retire those that fail.
detail: The assessment packet requires a live-analysis plan covering a minimum number of students, item and option functioning, subgroup and differential item functioning review, uncertainty, drift, quarantine and retirement (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/handoffs/g3-reading-v2-feedback-2026-07-16/assessment-item-agent.md`). The project's digest of a national reading study sets the bar: if performance differences reflect individual, social, linguistic or cultural variation rather than comprehension, the test is inadequate (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/skills/reading-science/DIGEST-rand-mr1465-2002.qmd`; RAND Reading Study Group 2002, https://www.rand.org/pubs/monograph_reports/MR1465.html). Revise options almost nobody picks, investigate items where weaker students beat stronger ones or stronger ones favour a distractor, and check subgroup fairness and drift.
against: These statistics need many responses: the retirement thresholds belong to a stage planned for 300 to 1,000 students (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0080-map-proxy-case-for-approval-2026-07-02-incept-map-proxy-approval-package.qmd`), and a diagnostic guide puts even basic calibration at 100 to 200 responses per item (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0154-diagnostic-assessment-brainlift.qmd`).

evidence.quote: Live-analysis plan covering minimum N, item and option functioning, subgroup/DIF review, uncertainty, drift, quarantine, and retirement.

Good comprehension assessments must be adaptable to individual, social, linguistic, and cultural variation; if performance differences reflect such variation rather than comprehension itself, the test is inadequate for the research/instructional agenda.

Difficulty index (proportion correct), discrimination index (point-biserial correlation with total score), and distractor analysis (proportion selecting each distractor, by ability group) are the minimum post-administration checks.
Negatively discriminating items — where weaker students outperform stronger students — are almost always flawed and should be investigated immediately.
A distractor selected more by high-performing students than low-performing students suggests the keyed answer is wrong or ambiguous.
Non-functioning distractors (selected by <5%) should be revised or the item reduced to fewer options.
item retirement (INFIT > 1.30 or pt-biserial < 0.20)
escalation are part of the lifecycle rather than optional cleanup.
an item’s difficulty may differ systematically across subgroups even when overall ability is matched.
Distractor-level data reviewed; non-functioning distractors (<5%) revised; negative-discrimination items flagged
J16-ASS-008: Treat predicted difficulty as a prior awaiting live calibration.
J16-ASS-009: Monitor live item functioning, fairness, and drift.
Non-functioning distractors (<5% pickup) get revised.
- The 14-dimension evaluation cannot assess Rasch model fit, item discrimination, or guessing behavior — these require empirical response data.
| INFIT mean square | 0.70 – 1.30 | Retire item |
| OUTFIT mean square | < 2.00 | Retire item |
| Point-biserial correlation | > 0.20 | Retire item |
| Empirical b vs provisional b | |Δb| < 0.5 logits | Accept; flag if > 0.5 |
Flag broken items (infit > 1.5)
D5.36 (distractor-response data review) requires live analytics on which distractors are actually chosen by real students; not derivable from authored JSON.
